paras: The Red Oak cotton pickers' cabin shooting was an attack in September 1903 in which unknown assailants fired a volley of shots into a cabin of Black cotton pickers on a farm near Red Oak, Texas. A Texas dispatch reported two men, George Hill and Jess Bruce, wounded but not seriously, while a Houston wire carried in Northern papers reported two men killed and two women wounded. No assailant was identified.
The cabin stood on the farm of J. T. Sullivan near Red Oak, and its occupants were there picking cotton.

According to a dispatch from Waxahachie dated September 10, an unknown party fired a volley of shots into the cabin at a late hour on Wednesday night. Hill was shot in the left shoulder with a pistol, and Bruce received a charge of shot in one arm. A Houston dispatch dated September 11 instead described cotton pickers sleeping in a hut who were fired on early that morning, with fifty shots fired.
The Houston wire stated that there was "no clew to the assailants." No report of an arrest, inquest or later investigation appears in the coverage.

In Texas, the Bryan Morning Eagle printed the Waxahachie item on September 11 under the headline "Shot Into House. Attempt Made to Assassinate Negro Cotton Pickers," a brief factual account without comment. The Houston wire reached papers outside the South the same day, appearing in the Walla Walla Evening Statesman as "Attack on Negro Cotton Pickers." The Stark County Democrat of Canton, Ohio, ran it on September 15 as a Scripps-McRae telegram headed "Negroes Killed by Unknown Assassins in Texas," and the Yale Expositor in Michigan carried a shortened version on September 25 as "Kill Negro Cotton Pickers."

The distant papers thus printed the deadlier version, while the Texas report, the only one to name the victims, described no deaths. None of the items assigned a motive or commented on the attack, and no coverage in the Black press was found.

The two accounts conflict on the toll: the Waxahachie dispatch reported two men wounded, not seriously, while the Houston wire reported two men killed and two women wounded. They also differ on timing, the local report placing the attack late on Wednesday night and the wire early on the morning of September 11. The Waxahachie report is the more specific, giving the farm owner, the victims' names and their wounds, but the coverage does not resolve the discrepancy.

bases: Unknown assailants fired a volley of shots into a cabin of Black cotton pickers, wounding (A1) or, in the wire version, killing and wounding occupants (A2, A3); no mob or band is named, and no accusation was attached.

A Texas dispatch (A1) and a Houston wire (A2, A3) agree that unknown parties fired into a dwelling of Black cotton pickers near Red Oak, but contradict each other on whether anyone was killed and on the sex of the wounded.

accounts.label: Waxahachie dispatch
accounts.gist: An unknown party fired a volley into a Black cabin on J. T. Sullivan's farm late Wednesday night; George Hill and Jess Bruce were wounded, not seriously.

accounts.label: Houston wire (Scripps-McRae)
accounts.gist: Unknown parties fired fifty shots into a hut where Black cotton pickers were sleeping early on Sept. 11, killing two men and wounding two women; there was no clue to the assailants.

Northern papers ran the Houston wire under headlines such as 'Attack on Negro Cotton Pickers' and 'NEGROES Killed by Unknown Assassins in Texas', without comment.
